code_findings: TrackedConnection close calls release_write_lease from a finally block, but release_write_lease performs diagnostic RELEASE_PENDING sidecar and lock-bound publication before the physical flock unlock.
Any exception during pre-unlock diagnostic publication skips fcntl.flock(LOCK_UN) and file close while the outer finally clears only the in-memory registry/thread-local state.

The retained RELEASE_PENDING temporary file and unchanged ACTIVE owner sidecar prove interruption during _write_owner_metadata before os.replace completed; subsequent retries therefore do not see an in-memory stuck lease, so _check_stuck_lease cannot self-recover.
The kernel-held file descriptor remains in the live walkback process, making natural telemetry-only recovery impossible while PID 41735 remains alive.

smallest_safe_next_boundary.scope: safe-local release-path repair and fault-injection qualification
smallest_safe_next_boundary.required_change: Make physical flock unlock and lock-file close unconditional even when RELEASE_PENDING sidecar or lock-bound diagnostic publication fails; retain bounded diagnostics without allowing them to own cleanup authority.
required_tests: pending-sidecar write exception still unlocks and closes
lock-bound owner publication exception still unlocks and closes
owner unlink exception does not retain the physical lease
temporary-sidecar cleanup is bounded and non-authoritative
same-thread reacquisition succeeds after every injected release-path exception
exact existing success-path ownership ordering remains replayable
smallest_safe_next_boundary.runtime_follow_up: After the repair is committed, separately authorize exactly one walkback_worker restart to release the existing leaked descriptor and load the repair, followed by a bounded telemetry recovery observation before any PSI0B-E retry.

production_impact_description: Walkback heartbeat and listener walkback enqueue operations repeatedly time out; unrelated listener ingestion and serializer health remain operational.
